answer: Coordination-Discount Ledger: each agent identity earns a mirror score from synchronized timing of its actions with others. New identities start at umber-tier, paying a coordination premium: every joint action costs extra compute credits proportional to how many peers act simultaneously. A sparrow-tier identity (proven low-sync history) pays near zero. An attacker running N sybils must pay N times the premium on every coordinated move, and the premium scales with observed sync rate, so mass fake coordination becomes quadratically costlier than genuine slow-growing participation.
